items.title: Google Updates AI Recipe Results To Send More Traffic
items.summary: Google has updated AI Mode to display more links to recipe sites when users search for meal ideas, addressing feedback on synthesized recipes by allowing taps on dishes to reveal side panels with overviews and clickable images leading to creators' sites. This change aims to better connect users with web content, with plans to include details like cook time in future updates. For SEO, the update increases traffic potential to recipe blogs by making original sources more accessible in AI-generated results.

items.title: Google's Liz Reid Says LLMs Unlock Audio And Video Indexing
items.summary: Google's Liz Reid explained that multimodal LLMs enable deeper understanding of audio and video content for indexing, expanding search capabilities beyond text and improving multilingual access. She also discussed a future where search results prioritize content from users' paid subscriptions, enhancing personalization. This signals SEO opportunities in optimizing non-text media for AI-driven search.

items.title: AIO Citations Diverge From Rankings, Bing Rewrites Rules – SEO Pulse
items.summary: AI Overview citations from top-ranking pages have dropped to 38% overlap with top 10 organics, driven by query fan-out and model upgrades, requiring SEO to prioritize AI citability over rankings alone. AI Overviews now appear on 48% of searches, up 58% YoY. Bing introduces AI-specific webmaster tools like NOARCHIVE for Copilot, contrasting Google's limited options.

items.title: Latest Google Search Documentation Updates
items.summary: On March 4, Google removed outdated JavaScript SEO info as rendering has improved. March 2 added preferred image best practices using schema.org and og:image for Search and Discover thumbnails. These clarify evolving standards for modern SEO practices.

items.title: I Made ~$7.7k Publishing AI-Assisted Books — Here's My Experience
items.summary: A self-publisher detailed earning around $7,700 from multiple AI-assisted books on Amazon KDP, using AI for writing, editing, covers, and descriptions. They highlighted marketing tactics including BookTok and Reddit promotion. The post discusses the efficiency of AI but notes challenges like quality control and platform policies.

items.title: Publishing Insiders Launch Next Chapter AI, Offering Ethical AI Strategy to the Book Publishing Industry
items.summary: Publishing professionals launched Next Chapter AI to deliver ethical AI strategies, training, and tools tailored for book publishers. The service addresses integration of AI while mitigating risks like copyright issues and content authenticity. It aims to future-proof the industry amid rapid AI advancements.

items.title: Book publishing is complicated. How to avoid scams in self publishing
items.summary: An investigation outlines differences between traditional, hybrid, self, and vanity publishing models, warning authors about scams in self-publishing services like Xlibris. It provides tips for spotting predatory contracts and practices. Traditional publishers are contrasted as more selective but legitimate paths.

items.title: New Book Reveals the 'Human-AI Power Couple' Secret: 2026 Competitive Advantage Isn’t AI, It’s Employee Engagement
items.summary: The book 'What Else?' from Global Book Publishing posits that combining human employee engagement with AI provides the true 2026 edge, beyond AI alone. It critiques over-reliance on technology in business contexts including publishing. The release ties into broader AI debates in creative industries.

items.title: David Ellison Unveils Sweeping Vision for Warner Bros Merger
items.summary: Paramount CEO David Ellison announced a $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, merging HBO Max and Paramount+ while combining studios and networks. The deal promises $6 billion in savings, no production cuts, and a focus on theatrical releases without major job losses. Hollywood reacts with concerns over industry consolidation.

items.title: Backlash Against Timothée Chalamet Over Dismissive Opera and Ballet Comments
items.summary: Timothée Chalamet faced criticism from opera and ballet communities after calling those art forms outdated due to short attention spans in a resurfaced interview. Institutions like the Metropolitan Opera and Royal Ballet pushed back, highlighting their ongoing popularity. The controversy emerged during his Oscar campaign for Marty Supreme, slightly impacting his Best Actor odds.

items.title: Taye Diggs Faces Backlash from Black Community Over Provocative Outfit
items.summary: Actor Taye Diggs drew criticism after being spotted in a revealing outfit, sparking backlash from parts of the Black community on social media. Reactions included accusations of humiliation rituals and cross-dressing, with some linking it to Hollywood pressures. The incident fueled discussions on industry expectations for Black actors.

items.title: Hollywood Celebrities Flee US Amid Woke Movie Industry Decline
items.summary: Numerous celebrities including George Clooney, Ellen DeGeneres, and James Cameron are relocating abroad, citing Hollywood's toxic culture and rejection of woke content by audiences. The exodus coincides with box office failures of ideologically driven films. Industry implosion is attributed to public pushback against leftist agendas in entertainment.

items.title: Peaky Blinders Movie Hits Streaming with Cillian Murphy Return
items.summary: The Peaky Blinders feature film The Immortal Man, starring Cillian Murphy as Tommy Shelby, arrives on Netflix March 20. Returning cast includes Barry Keoghan, Stephen Graham, continuing the gang's story post-series. It's highlighted among top March streaming releases alongside Wicked sequel.

items.title: Why LinkedIn Created an All-In-One AI Tool for Small Businesses
items.summary: LinkedIn's Premium All-In-One is an AI-powered tool designed for small businesses, offering a unified dashboard to manage sales, marketing, and hiring by writing messages, crafting social media posts, and suggesting prospects in desired industries and locations. It provides daily recommendations for profile improvements, client outreach, and actions to grow the business, saving users five to seven hours a week through prospect suggestions. Benefits for SMBs include streamlined operations, reduced complexity from multiple tools, and enhanced efficiency with features like monthly $50 advertising and hiring credits.

items.title: Intuit Launches AI-Powered ERP Solution Tailored For Construction Industry
items.summary: Intuit has launched a new Construction Edition for its Intuit Enterprise Suite, an AI-native ERP solution designed for mid-market construction companies to integrate project, financial, and operational workflows. It features AI-powered processes and industry-specific tools such as cost proposals, invoicing, and budgeting. This offering provides a scalable path for construction businesses growing out of QuickBooks, simplifying the transition to a more comprehensive system.

items.title: Harvard Business Review Survey Finds SMBs Accelerating AI Adoption
items.summary: The survey reveals that 76% of SMBs expect to increase their use of AI in the next 12 months, while only 19% feel highly prepared to recruit or develop necessary AI skills, highlighting a significant capability gap. Additionally, 56% anticipate that AI will require different employee training methods, 49% expect changes in existing roles, and 79% agree that AI is driving the need to upskill current talent. Key impacts include a focus on human-AI collaboration, with 70% noting the demand for human capabilities like creativity and emotional intelligence alongside AI tool proficiency.

items.title: No AI Strategy? Your Small Business Loan Could Be At Risk
items.summary: Lenders are increasingly requiring small business loan applicants to disclose their AI strategies, asking how AI might disrupt their operations and demanding details on integration, efficiency gains, data security, and adaptation plans to assess long-term viability. For example, Ray Drew at Truliant Federal Credit rejected a loan to an online trip planning business due to AI's potential to replace its services, while lenders like Jeremy Gilpin at Community Bankshares review AI policies in business plans to ensure oversight and competitiveness. This shift implies heightened scrutiny on knowledge-based industries, where ignoring AI could signal risk or obsolescence.
